entities.title: The README's table still describes requirements "with their marks"
entities.summary: The README describes requirements.md as answering "what it does, as capabilities and features, with their marks", but the marks were knowledge-driven development's and were taken out of the templates.
entities.expected: The README's row for requirements.md describes what the template now holds: capabilities, features and use cases, what is out of scope and the open questions, without knowledge-driven development's marks.
entities.observed: The row reads "What it does, as capabilities and features, with their marks"; requirements.md itself no longer mentions marks.

origin.description: Found while bringing processes in line with human-assisted software development.

entities.title: business-plan.md puts its Purpose guidance above the heading
entities.summary: In business-plan.md the guidance comment for Purpose sits above the "## Purpose" heading, and the line after the title is a comment rather than the source-of-truth line; every other template puts the source-of-truth line straight after the title and each section's guidance under its heading.
entities.expected: As in the other eleven templates and as the README says: the first line after the title is "**Source of truth:** ...", and the Purpose guidance follows the "## Purpose" heading.
entities.observed: The title is followed by a comment explaining the source-of-truth line, then "**Source of truth:** here.", then the comment "One paragraph. What this deployable does for the business ...", then "## Purpose" with nothing under it.

origin.description: Found while bringing processes in line with human-assisted software development.
